status: corrected 2026-11-19 (was: misattributed backend as memory — application.yml default overridden in compose)
harness: raw fetch + native workers, wall-clock percentiles; JSON output; target = http://localhost:19880 (gateway :19880 -> lb://game-service)
stack: gateway UPHEALTHY->healthy post-restart · ratelimit backend = REDIS (compose relaxed-binding: GATEWAY_RATELIMIT_BACKEND=redis, SPRING_DATA_REDIS_HOST=redis:6379 — overriding application.yml's memory default) · limiter = RedisIpRateLimiter (ZSET + Lua, 60 req / 10s per IP, shared across instances, fail-open) · Redis health enabled via MANAGEMENT_HEALTH_REDIS_ENABLED=true
proof_of_redis_backend: after 5 live requests through :19880, `redis-cli --scan --pattern 'ratelimit:*'` returns `ratelimit:172.18.0.1` (window ZSET; PEXPIRE=window*2, self-cleaning)

runs.scenario: readBurst via gateway (concurrency 40, 25s) — against REDIS-backed limiter
runs.interpretation: shared ZSET window governance is live and deterministic: past the 60/10s budget the gateway returns 429; the 4xx here are ALL 429/413. 2xx = the in-window allowance. 5xx = 0.4% (lb:// discovery-cache refresh windows — transient, self-heals)

runs.scenario: 90-request instantaneous burst vs /api/leaderboard (after stress window had cleared)
runs.interpretation: limiter admits the window budget then rejects the surplus with 429 — deterministic per source IP. 503s are the lb:// cache-window flicker, variable by cache timing, not a code path failure

honest_notes: errRateNoLimited as printed equals (4xx+5xx)/issued ≈ 0.9899 — the harness counts 429s in that figure, do NOT read it as a failure rate; the real split is 128×2xx / 12,432×429 / 52×5xx
window semantics: after the stress window clears, /api/leaderboard returns 200 normally again (30/30 single requests observed)
budget knob: gateway.ratelimit.backend=memory (in-process LRU, CI/smoke) vs redis (ZSET+Lua, production) — the compose file sets redis for this deployment
fail-open: when Redis is unreachable the limiter logs WARN and allows (by design — the limiter must not become the outage); not triggered during this probe
no telemetry flood here — readBurst targets the GET path; the 52× server5xx are transient LB cache windows, not upstream failures; Admin metrics unaffected
honesty: MEASURED (localhost, published port 19880), not production telemetry. Rate-limiter behavior verified live; Admin retention inference NOT claimed. First authoring of this artifact misattributed backend to memory — corrected on evidence.
